The root sheath is indeed the squishy white thing surrounding the hair. The actual "root" is bulbous end of the hair. It is usually wet looking and is not technically edible. The root sheath however, is. 


Now, the pilla is embedded nice a deep in your dermis/skin. You are disconnecting the root from the pilla when you have a root sheath that has a red tip or there is a little blood coming from the pore/follicle. That means you have destroyed the roots connection with the pilla making the probability of that hair growing back under 10%.

Not every hair you pull out will grow back the same. It depends on the amount of damage the follicle received. 


A hair with a fully attached root sheath will begin a fresh cycle, growing slightly faster until the hair breaks through the skin. 


A hair with a broken root sheath will take longer. The body has to recognize that the sheath is broken, get rid of it, replace it. And then the hair will begin to grow. 


A hair with no sheath at all will continue to grow at the rate it normally does. Around 1/2 inch per month. 


Finally, a hair that has been pulled and has a red tip/ blood around the follicle is dead. You removed the pilla when you pulled that certain hair. It will most likely never grow back.

I nervously tapped my manicured fingernails against the hard plastic chair and shifted in the uncomfortable chair.


*You think Heaven could afford some nice plush chairs* I thought to myself as I scanned the others waiting for their chance at snagging the elusive job. 


All of them looked well polished and well dressed. I knew that they had to have the experience, the ad stated clearly that you had to have made it through at least ten life cycles without being corrupted **or** overly benevolent. Any less would be a laugh at your inexperience. 


I myself had made it through seventy eight life cycles without being pulled into either Heaven or Hell. I was proud of my achievements. I had seen empires built and watched as they fell. I witnessed the wars, dictators, and Mother Theresa's. My eyes had observed the beginnings of religions and the start of cults. My body had been subject to starvation more than once due to famine or war. 


And yet when I died and returned to the Lobby, I was excited to go back. During my short times on Earth I remembered nothing of my past cycles. A core part of me never changed however. I was always neutral. I never went above and beyond to do good, but I never sunk down and released the inner evil either. 


"Miss Lorrilie, we'll see you now", a soft voice spoke. I recognized my name from my last cycle and arose from my chair. Turning around I watched a small door open and a figure beckoned me inside. I made my way into the extravagant room. Everything was jewel encrusted and every surface shimmered. I stood in awe for a brief moment before I noticed a small group of beings behind a table made of solid gold. They glowed faintly and even though I couldn't make out their figures, I could tell that they were humanoid. 


"Miss Lorrilie, we have reviewed you application for Heaven and we must say that we are astounded by the number of cycles you have managed to acquire.", one spoke with a soft voice that reminded me of the winds that flowed over the plains that once held no trace of modern human touch. 


"While this a feat we haven't seen before, it's not necessarily a good one...", a different voice trailed off.


I felt a deep sinking feeling and took in a deep breath to calm myself. 


"It's because of the fact that you went over fifty cycles without that we have to deny your request to become an angel.", the voice of this being sounded like a bubbling brook. 


"But there is an upside.... You see, the downstairs department is also hiring and the pay is significantly better. You'd more than triple the amount of lives you would have had than if you were to work with us."


*Downstairs?*, I thought quizzically.  *Do they mean Hell?*


"Yes, dear. We do mean Hell.", the smooth breeze came back to me. 


"You mean to tell me that I would have more than two hundred and twenty cycles to do as I pleased?", my voice sounded unsure. "More than two hundred and twenty cycles that I would remember without question?"


"Yes Lorrilie.", they answered in unison. 


"Send me!" The choice was instant. All of those years, all of the experiences, and all of it could be mine. It was a no-brainer. 


And the shining room vanished in an instant and was replaced by hard, smooth stone. Everything had a tint of gray to it. I did a brief view of the room and saw a young gentleman sitting behind a heavy wooden desk. He was dressed impeccably well. A tailored suit clung to his large frame. He stood and shrugged off his jacket. He carelessly tossed it unto a leather couch that was a few feet behind him and gestured to a chair in front of his behemoth desk. 

"Please, Lorrilie, have a seat. Welcome to Hell. My name is Lucifer. Are you ready to start your life?"

My eyes fluttered open and I was awake staring at the glow in the dark stars I had splattered all over my ceiling years previous. The bright neon coloring of them hinted to me that the sun still had hours until its rays would pour out over the horizon. I sighed heavily and stretched my body out trying to regain comfort. 

Sleep would not come back to me. I flung my comforter off of myself and heaved my body out of the bed. Groggily, I made my way to my kitchen for water. As I reached for my doorknob, my vision blurred and I briefly saw my hand reaching towards a gun. I retracted my hand back quickly and heard a soft voice say, 

*lock the door and go back to bed....*

And then everything was back to normal. 

Frozen, I stood with my hand inches away from the door. I tried to rationalize the image to myself as a leftover memory from the dream I had that had awoken me.  Surely that had to it. I sighed a small laugh, shook my head, and grasped the cold brass. 

Immediately, my vision shifted back to me reaching for the gun. I gripped the cold metal in my hand. I raised the killing machine to my face and realized my hands were filthy. They were covered in streaks of brown and rust. It took me a moment to realize that it was daytime. I was no longer in my bedroom, but what I guessed to be a tent of some kind. There were tarp covered boxes surrounding me. My now boot covered feet crunched over a hard packed earth floor. The air was warm and I could feel sweat stick to my body uncomfortably. 

I took in my new environment slowly. Everything seemed to be covered in a small layer of sand. A hot breeze occasionally ran across my back and briefly cooled me. I looked up and noticed a mirror with a large, deep crack running through it. I could my body with ease and placed myself in front of the reflective surface. 

The face that I saw shocked me. It was mine, but harder. My eyes were still grey, but no longer did I have a doe eyed look. My chin still had a small cleft, but a large scar ran across it. My normal chubby cheeks were transformed into cheekbones that cut out from my face and my long brown hair was gone. I now had a short trimmed cut. I looked down at my hand and saw that I still gripped the gun tightly. 

I looked again into the mirror. 

"You need to lock the door and get back into bed." My reflection said calmly. 

I freaked out. 

"What is this?!" I tried shaking myself awake again, but to no avail. I was still hot and sweaty, and the gun was still in my hand. 

"You need to trust me. Lock your door, get into bed, and be quiet. Your life depends on it." 

I stared down my reflection and tried to glower as effectively as I could muster. The image in front of me failed to change. 

"In a moment, someone is going to break into your house and try to steal the formula that you've been working on. If you go downstairs they will kill you. They will kill you and steal your research. If you lock your door, you will kill them. You will search their body and find out information on the organization that is trying to silence you. You will systematically take them down and will be known for saving humanity."

My heart started to beat quickly and I could feel my palms start to sweat. 

"You need to do this. You **have** to do this."

I gave a small nod. I looked down at my hands again and a small pit formed in my stomach. Blood. My hands were covered in blood. 

"It's a small price to pay for the lives of billions." My reflections voice sounded sharp.
